After the first exodus, there were many posts in /v/introductions by self-proclaimed "former lurkers" that were excited to start getting involved. There were even a few askvoat threads in the same vein. All of this suggests that the average former redditor was a lurker.

Now, everything is different. It's the active users and the mods who are leaving. Already, reddit's post quality has taken a nose dive as a result. Reddit user rahmad explains that this will lead to fast decline of users. The average redditor doesn't care if mods have good modding tools, but they sure as hell care if the quality goes down or some subreddits go private.

Honestly, I think redditors are flattering themselves a little too much. Most people who use reddit are "casual" users, just there for the funny/cool content. Sure, people have left but new people will also discover reddit. Long ago it stopped being a community for open discussion. Now it is a site that has amassed such a large userbase that the relatively few who leave will not really disrupt the day to day operation. Just browsing reddit the past couple of days, I haven't seen more than a couple mentions of what went on.

I think the idea is that even if the vast majority of users continue to use reddit casually, it is the minority of redditers (the mods and content creaters) who keep the site popular. All it would take to change reddit permanently would be the mods leaving. And it is that crowd (the users who are involved in the politics of reddit) that would be the users who leave.
